lines.speaker: sol
lines.text: You! Yes, you. How would you feel about becoming the founding champion of an event I invented twelve seconds ago?

lines.speaker: Protagonist
lines.text: Depends. What's the event?

lines.speaker: sol
lines.text: A treasure hunt! Somewhere here there's a plastic Psyduck. Find it, win a juice. Ignore that I lost it myself.

lines.speaker: Protagonist
lines.text: Is wearing a bikini in the middle of town part of the rules?

lines.speaker: sol
lines.text: Nope. That's just Tuesday. The prize involves absolutely no mandatory swimwear.

lines.speaker: marina
lines.text: Sol, you left the clue cards where the tide can reach them.

lines.speaker: sol
lines.text: An aquatic difficulty modifier! ...Okay, not excellent. Will you two help me move them?

lines.speaker: Protagonist
lines.text: You're good at making accidents sound like adventures.

lines.speaker: sol
lines.text: Only harmless ones. Come on, we've got a duck to find.

choices.label: Help turn the chaos into a real game
choices.reply: You organized my nonsense without making it boring. Are you some kind of wizard?

choices.label: Ask whether everyone actually wants to play
choices.reply: Oh. You mean ask before I recruit half the neighborhood? ...Fair. That is a good rule.

choices.label: Tell her the outfit makes her hard to ignore
choices.reply: Honey, I came dressed to be seen. But can you keep up with me?

events.title: The Worst Party in Neo Harbor

lines.speaker: sol
lines.text: I booked an arcade party. Eight people RSVP'd. Two came. One is here to fix the pinball machine.

lines.speaker: Protagonist
lines.text: So we're down to one?

lines.speaker: sol
lines.text: Two, if you stay. Three if we count the technician's emotional-support screwdriver.

lines.speaker: yuna
lines.text: I didn't know this was a party. The flyer said 'unannounced surprise experience.'

lines.speaker: sol
lines.text: I was trying to make it irresistible.

lines.speaker: Protagonist
lines.text: It was also impossible to know what you were signing up for.

lines.speaker: sol
lines.text: Ugh. You're right. I keep treating 'surprise' as the same thing as 'fun.'

lines.speaker: yuna
lines.text: We could play a silly draft game. No audience required.

lines.speaker: sol
lines.text: ...Actually, that sounds nice.

choices.label: Host one ridiculous game with her
choices.reply: Two players, two sodas and the worst deck names imaginable. I'm having more fun than I planned.

choices.label: Encourage clearer invitations next time
choices.reply: I'm scared they'll say no if they know what they're getting. That's my problem, not theirs.

choices.label: Suggest a low-key date instead of a spectacle
choices.reply: A date? Wait, you're serious? Let's find out whether I can flirt without a microphone.

openingByFlag.sol_help: I still have that paper trophy from our duck hunt. I booked an arcade party. Eight people RSVP'd. Two came.
openingByFlag.sol_ask: I asked for RSVPs this time. Eight people said yes to an arcade party. Two came.
openingByFlag.sol_banter: Remember when you said I was impossible to ignore? Turns out my arcade flyer was easy to ignore. Eight RSVP'd; two came.

lines.speaker: alma
lines.text: Sol's been here three hours. She's ordered one lemonade and made seven festival plans.

lines.speaker: sol
lines.text: Six. Number four involved fireworks in a public library. Legally unsound.

lines.speaker: Protagonist
lines.text: Why are you keeping so busy?

lines.speaker: sol
lines.text: Last year I tried to run a summer festival alone. Sponsors fell through. I cancelled it and told everybody it was 'rescheduled.'

lines.speaker: Protagonist
lines.text: You never told them what happened?

lines.speaker: sol
lines.text: I didn't want people who believed in me to find out I'd failed.

lines.speaker: alma
lines.text: Half those people would've helped. You never asked.

lines.speaker: sol
lines.text: I know. Asking feels scarier than announcing something exciting.

lines.speaker: Protagonist
lines.text: You don't need a festival to make people want to be here.

lines.speaker: sol
lines.text: That's lovely. I'm going to need time to believe it.

choices.label: Stay for lemonade and let her talk
choices.reply: You didn't try to fix me with a pep talk. I noticed. Thanks.

choices.label: Ask who she wants on the team this time
choices.reply: Not who'll clap for me. Who'll actually say 'stop' when I need it. Yeah, I know who to ask.

choices.label: Offer to be there even on a boring day
choices.reply: I may hold you to that. My definition of boring is a little experimental.

openingByFlag.sol_small: The tiny arcade night cheered her up. And now Sol's been here three hours planning the next festival.
openingByFlag.sol_clear: Sol sent perfectly clear invitations this time. She's still been here for three hours planning the follow-up.
openingByFlag.sol_date: Sol's been here three hours rehearsing something about a date. Personally, I'd like my table back.

lines.speaker: jun
lines.text: I can't approve the riverside festival if the safety team says the water is unsafe.

lines.speaker: sol
lines.text: I know. I've already written the cancellation notice.

lines.speaker: Protagonist
lines.text: You sound like you're waiting for us to talk you out of it.

lines.speaker: sol
lines.text: For two minutes, I was. Then I thought about the kids getting home after dark.

lines.speaker: jun
lines.text: That is a responsible decision, Sol.

lines.speaker: sol
lines.text: Please don't compliment me like that. It makes me feel like a grown-up.

lines.speaker: Protagonist
lines.text: You can still make this weekend good.

lines.speaker: sol
lines.text: The café has an indoor table. The arcade owes me a favor. No river, no big crowd—just people who want to come.

lines.speaker: jun
lines.text: I'll help write the notice. In readable font this time.

lines.speaker: sol
lines.text: Careful, Jun. One more sensible choice and you're on my planning committee.

choices.label: Help her build a small indoor event
choices.reply: I kept waiting for the grand version to save everything. Maybe the small version was real all along.

choices.label: Say you respect her decision to cancel
choices.reply: It felt awful. I also know it was right. Both things can be true.

choices.label: Ask her out after the event, no costumes required
choices.reply: No costumes? Cruel. But yes. Just the two of us sounds pretty amazing.

openingByFlag.sol_listen: Sol spent a day thinking about the festival. Unfortunately, the waterfront safety report is not encouraging.
openingByFlag.sol_team: Sol finally recruited a festival team. As a member of that team, I need to tell her the waterfront is unsafe.
openingByFlag.sol_ordinary: I wish this were an ordinary scheduling call. The waterfront won't be safe for her festival this weekend.

lines.speaker: sol
lines.text: I brought two drinks, a blanket, and absolutely no activities. How's that for personal growth?

lines.speaker: Protagonist
lines.text: I'm suspicious. Where's the hidden scavenger hunt?

lines.speaker: sol
lines.text: Under that tree. Kidding! Look at your face.

lines.speaker: Protagonist
lines.text: The indoor party went well. The kids stayed for hours.

lines.speaker: sol
lines.text: And when they left, I didn't feel I'd failed. People can have fun and still go home. Who knew?

lines.speaker: Protagonist
lines.text: What made you want to meet tonight?

lines.speaker: sol
lines.text: I'm good at asking people to do something. I wanted to try asking you to be somewhere with me. No audience.

lines.speaker: Protagonist
lines.text: You don't have to entertain me.

lines.speaker: sol
lines.text: I know. I still want to make you laugh, though. That's different.

lines.speaker: sol
lines.text: I know what I'd call tonight: my favorite plan yet. But I want to hear what you want us to be, without making the answer into a game.

choices.label: Tell her you want to be with her beyond summer
choices.reply: Then I have one scary plan: we keep showing up for each other, even when nothing special happens.

choices.label: Promise to make ridiculous memories as friends
choices.reply: Deal. First memory: I sat still for an entire sunset. Nobody will believe you.

choices.label: Tell her she doesn't need to decide tonight
choices.reply: The kindest non-answer I've ever heard. Stay a little longer? I think I can enjoy not knowing.

openingByFlag.sol_safe: Our little indoor party was a hit. I brought two drinks, a blanket and absolutely no activities.
openingByFlag.sol_boundary: Cancelling the river plan was right. People understood. I brought two drinks and no activities tonight.
openingByFlag.sol_after: I remembered you asked me out after the party. I brought two drinks and no activities.

events.title: The Dress Code Is Common Sense

lines.speaker: sol
lines.text: Alma, that coffee machine sounds like it's trying to evolve.

lines.speaker: alma
lines.text: Steam valve. Also, did you just come in from the river?

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: A trail of wet footprints crosses the café tiles. Sol follows it back to her own sandals.

lines.speaker: sol
lines.text: Oh. That's me. Please tell me nobody slipped.

lines.speaker: Protagonist
lines.text: There's a dry mat by the door. I can help with the floor.

lines.speaker: alma
lines.text: Mop's under the sink. I'll fix the coffee machine while you take care of that.

lines.speaker: sol
lines.text: Deal. I'll put a little wet-shoes sign by the entrance too. Consider it my first useful decoration of the day.

lines.speaker: alma
lines.text: Keep clear of the cord and we're friends.

choices.label: Help make the café safer
choices.reply: I'll get the mop. And don't worry, I'll leave the coffee machine to a professional.

choices.label: Point out Alma respected her style and set a clear boundary
choices.reply: She didn't ask me to change clothes, just to leave a dry floor behind. Fair enough.

openingByFlag.sol_help: I promised to be practical after the duck hunt, Alma. Your coffee machine is testing my resolve.
openingByFlag.sol_ask: I asked before planning anything here, Alma. I just didn't ask what that noise from the coffee machine was.
openingByFlag.sol_banter: The duck hunt survived the swimsuit. I'm not sure your coffee machine will survive the afternoon.

lines.speaker: marina
lines.text: The landing's closed past the rail. The water's moving too fast for games.

lines.speaker: sol
lines.text: I bought forty water balloons. Forty. And the river decides to be dramatic first.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The warning sign rattles against a post. Someone from the ferry crew tightens the rope across the wet steps.

lines.speaker: Protagonist
lines.text: The park shelter still has dry tables and plenty of room.

lines.speaker: sol
lines.text: Not exactly the thrilling river party I'd advertised.

lines.speaker: marina
lines.text: Then change the location. Nobody needs to get wet to enjoy the afternoon.

lines.speaker: sol
lines.text: A dry-land accuracy contest, then. I'll ask the crew where we can set up without blocking the path.

lines.speaker: Protagonist
lines.text: We could keep score using the spare deck boxes.

lines.speaker: sol
lines.text: Yes! I'll write the teams up. Nobody goes near the landing.

choices.label: Help run a safe dry-land game
choices.reply: I'll bring the targets. You take the balloons. Marina, keep an eye on the landing for us.

choices.label: Thank Marina for making the difficult call
choices.reply: Marina made the right call. I'll send everyone the new location before they set out.

openingByFlag.sol_small: The arcade party sounded fun, Sol. The ferry party needs a change of venue. Look at that current.
openingByFlag.sol_clear: Thanks for sending an actual itinerary, Sol. I'm afraid the river hasn't read it.
openingByFlag.sol_date: I won't interrupt your plans, Sol. I just need to tell you the landing isn't safe for the ferry party.
